title: Winona vs FutureClinic: an HRT subscription from its own pharmacy, or a prescription to yours
summary: Winona vs FutureClinic compares menopause HRT cost per month (Winona patches from $149/mo) with a $40 FutureClinic visit and using your own pharmacy.
body_markdown:
Both Winona and FutureClinic use physicians only to treat perimenopause and[menopause](https://futureclinic.com/blog/menopause-treatment-online-hrt-from-a-doctor) by message, differing in how you get your medicine. Winona is a strong option when you want compounded hormones bundled into a recurring monthly order from[its own pharmacies](https://futureclinic.com/blog/why-your-online-doctor-shouldnt-be-selling-you-the-medicine) , starting at $149 a month for an estrogen patch and $39 a month for progesterone capsules (as of October 2026). FutureClinic connects you with a physician for $40 for the best-fit doctor (or typically $20 to $100 for a chosen doctor) with no subscription required, sending any prescription to the pharmacy you choose if your doctor decides it's right for you.


On FutureClinic, no form gets approved in bulk. A specific doctor reads your whole case and answers you with a Human Signature, a short video or voice note recorded live for you. You can message the same doctor over time in that chat, ask them to help with other problems in their specialty, and have every FutureClinic doctor you see work from[one medical record](https://futureclinic.com/blog/one-online-doctor-for-everything-vs-condition-apps) .


## How do Winona and FutureClinic compare side by side?


Feature Winona FutureClinic


Who treats you Board-certified physicians ("We only hire board-certified physicians") State-licensed physicians (MD, DO or MBBS), never a nurse practitioner or physician assistant


What you pay (as of October 2026) Free consult; patches from $149/mo, creams from $89/mo, tablets from $54/mo, progesterone from $39/mo $40 best-fit doctor, or chosen doctor (typically $20 to $100); optional membership


Subscription required? Yes, per product No subscription required


Where medicine comes from Winona's two 503A compounding pharmacies The pharmacy you choose, retail or mail-order


Insurance Does not work directly with insurance Cash-pay visit; insurance or coupon at pharmacy; prior authorization help


What else the doctor treats Menopause HRT and a few non-HRT creams Other problems in their specialty; every FutureClinic doctor you see works from your one medical record


How you reach them Messaging on bywinona.com (typically 24 to 48 hours); no AI app Messaging on futureclinic.com or your AI app (typically a few hours, almost always same day or next)


What you get back Treatment plan and compounded refills Written plan and Human Signature; prescriptions or discounted labs when your doctor orders them


## Do you want a menopause subscription, or a doctor one to one?


Menopause care changes over time. Messaging the same doctor across visits builds trust so you can try treatments together and track progress: adjusting an estradiol dose if night sweats return, swapping a patch that irritates your skin, and deciding when to step up or down.


Your FutureClinic doctor has one incentive: helping you. FutureClinic sells no medicines, and your doctor earns nothing extra for any prescription or test, so they never upsell lab panels or drugs. You never stay subscribed month after month to keep your medicine. With no house formulary, your doctor can prescribe whichever brand or generic fits you to the pharmacy you choose, if your doctor decides it's right for you.


On[Winona's FAQ page](https://bywinona.com/faq) , care covers menopause HRT for women 35 to 59 in 37 states and Puerto Rico, plus non-HRT creams for adults 18+ like its compounded Sildenafil Arousal Cream. Winona also[launched a menopause research initiative](https://medcitynews.com/2026/06/winona-launches-menopause-research-initiative/) in June 2026, though no general medicine was found. On FutureClinic, an internal medicine or family doctor managing your HRT can also treat other problems in their specialty, such as cholesterol, blood pressure, or thyroid care. FutureClinic has over 300 doctors. Generalists and specialists practice across more than 60 specialties, and every FutureClinic doctor you see works from your one medical record.


## How do monthly HRT subscriptions compare with using your own pharmacy?


Winona suits women 35 to 59 who want its compounded products bundled into a monthly plan. Its[homepage](https://bywinona.com/) offers a free visit and free, unlimited follow-ups on a plan. Two 503A compounding pharmacies Winona owns in El Dorado Hills, California, and Twin Falls, Idaho fill and ship orders. On[Winona's product page](https://bywinona.com/product) , as of October 2026, estrogen patches start from $149 a month, progesterone capsules from $39 a month, body creams at $89, and tablets at $54. Refills ship every 28 or 84 days; you can pause up to 90 days or cancel any time (24-hour refund window).


That price assumes you stay subscribed every month to keep getting the medicine: an estrogen patch from $149 a month plus progesterone from $39 a month totals at least $188 a month, or $2,256 over a year (as of October 2026).


FutureClinic works[per visit](https://futureclinic.com/blog/telehealth-subscriptions-vs-paying-a-doctor-per-visit-yearly-cost) with no subscription needed. Pay $40 for the best-fit doctor, or pick a specific doctor at their listed price, typically $20 to $100. If your doctor decides it's right for you, your prescription goes to the pharmacy you choose, including retail and mail-order pharmacies that deliver to your door. A text link lets you pick the pharmacy with a discount coupon for the best cash price, or use insurance at the pharmacy, with prior authorization help when needed. For a stable medicine, a doctor can prescribe several months at once when they judge it safe. Most doctors also offer an optional membership (typically $25 to $100 a month, median $50) for unlimited care with that doctor, cancel any time.
